note: Resync wave (runtime/remote) of the worktree-teardown/worktree-logic/worktree-removal-safety/cross-platform-path/ssh-config/terminal-stream-protocol modules first harvested at 143c36e (and, for worktree-teardown, at the later c3620f095 it was actually pulled from) to upstream v1.4.200. Entries with `supersedes` replace the same nexusPath in orca-143c36e.json, whose entries are marked superseded. Several entries in this wave are 'checked, no code changed' resyncs: the ported Nexus subset was already byte-identical to upstream, or upstream's delta lives entirely in code Nexus deliberately does not carry — each such entry's changeSummary says why. Not resynced on purpose: killAllProcessesForWorktree's Force Delete escape hatch (#11960, allowUnverifiedStop) and its structured-agent-session sweep / cross-host graph matching — Nexus's mission-runtime-termination.ts is a from-scratch reimplementation of the same physical-exit-before-replacement invariant for mission authority (not worktree PTY teardown), and weakening that invariant into an advisory check would allow split-brain mission authority. worktreePathComparisonKey/dedupeWorktreesByPath (new relay-listing exports on the areWorktreePathsEqual extraction) and gssapiAuthentication/parseSshConfigAliasClaims (new ssh-config-parser exports) also stay out — unused by anything in Nexus.

files.changeSummary: Resync check only, no code ported: this file shares no code with worktree-teardown.ts — it is a from-scratch reimplementation of physical-exit-before-replacement for mission authority, not worktree PTY teardown. Upstream added a 4th structured-agent-session sweep, cross-host graph matching (resolvedWorktreeId/resolvedConnectionId/resolvedRuntimeEnvironmentId), and an allowUnverifiedStop Force Delete escape hatch (#11960) that warns and proceeds instead of throwing when a stop cannot be proven. Deliberately not ported: the escape hatch would weaken the invariant into an advisory check, letting two sessions claim authority over one mission (split-brain).

Upstream split areWorktreePathsEqual out of worktree-logic.ts into src/main/ipc/worktree-path-comparison.ts (originalPath at the 143c36e pin), which also grew worktreePathComparisonKey and dedupeWorktreesByPath for relay/listing dedup — unused by Nexus, not ported. Brought forward: swapped the private looksLikeWindowsPath regex for the already-ported shared isWindowsAbsolutePathLike (removes a real duplicate upstream also removed) and extracted normalizeWindowsWorktreePathForComparison for parity. No behavioral change (the regex was byte-identical to isWindowsAbsolutePathLike).

Checked, no code changed: upstream's only delta (two new keys, cliProvenance/creatorProvenance, added to its ORCA WorktreeMeta sanitization array) lives entirely in the meta-update surface Nexus does not carry — WorktreeRecord provenance is main-owned via WorktreeStateStore CAS, so there is no legacy-evidence branch to extend. Header pin bumped to record the check.
Checked, no test behavior changed: upstream's only delta is an unrelated import path move (GitWorktreeInfo relocated to shared/worktree/types). Header pin bumped to record the check.

Checked, no code changed: the only helper in the Nexus subset (isWindowsAbsolutePathLike) is byte-identical upstream, despite the file growing substantially (WSL UNC aliasing, NFC comparison folding, createNormalizedPathInsideOrEqualMatcher, etc. — all unused, still deferred to a future remote/WSL harvest). Header pin bumped to record the check.

Checked, no code changed: this mapping (inherited from orca-143c36e.json) is a conceptual adaptation, not a literal port — ssh-path.ts implements remote-FS containment (normalizeSshRemotePath/resolveSshPathInsideRoot), unrelated to what ssh-config-path-expansion.ts actually changed upstream (the __PROGRAMDATA__ token fix, which has no counterpart in this file's logic and was instead ported to src/main/remote/ssh/ssh-config-path-expansion.ts below, this file's literal port target). Header pin bumped to record the check.

Brought forward OpenSSH's first-value-wins semantics for a single-valued directive repeated in one Host block (hostname/user/port/proxyjump now use ??= instead of =) — a real correctness bug fix, ported into Nexus's simpler per-block model (Nexus has no cross-block cascading match like real OpenSSH/orca, so only the within-block half of the fix applies). Not ported: the gssapiAuthentication field (Nexus has no GSSAPI auth path) and parseSshConfigAliasClaims (new upstream export; nothing in Nexus consumes alias-claim detection yet).
Added a case for the new first-value-wins behavior (repeated Port/User in one Host block keeps the first). Still a Nexus-authored concept test, not a literal upstream port.

Brought the __PROGRAMDATA__ token expansion fix: Windows ssh -G prints it unexpanded, and passing it through as a literal misses with ENOENT — indistinguishable from 'no host is known there', silently hiding a site-managed known_hosts, including one holding a rotated key that should have produced a mismatch. Adapted: splits the remainder on both path separators before join(), the same portable technique this file already used for its ~/ branch, instead of upstream's raw join(programData, rest), which is only correct when actually running on Windows.
Added cases for the __PROGRAMDATA__ fix: substitution, left-alone-when-unset (never guessed), and the startsWith-collision guard (a filename that merely begins with the token).

Full-file resync (direct copy). Brought decodeTerminalStreamJson's payload-size cap (8 MiB) and structural/nesting limits (a genuine DoS-prevention fix — a giant or deeply-nested JSON frame previously reached JSON.parse uncapped) and the opcodes added since 143c36e (Ack, ClaimViewport, OutputSpan, SetOutputPaused, WriteUnavailable) as type surface only — none are wired to anything in Nexus, kept so this shared module stays a faithful copy of the wire format. Requires the new src/shared/json-text-structure-limit.ts dependency (also added in this wave).
Full-file resync (direct copy). Brought the two new upstream cases: Ack frame round-trip, and rejecting excessive JSON nesting before JSON.parse is ever called (spy-verified).
New dependency of the resynced terminal-stream-protocol.ts (structural-token and nesting-depth admission scan, single-pass, string-aware). Direct copy; Nexus statement style only.
Direct copy of upstream's test file; Nexus statement style only.

Checked, no code changed: this production session wrapper only uses the Output/Resized/Subscribe opcodes and the frame shape, neither touched by the JSON size/structure limits or the new opcodes added to the underlying protocol module. Header pin bumped to record the check.
Checked, no test changed: session-wrapper tests exercise only the opcodes/frame shape unaffected by this wave's protocol changes.
